decision.summary: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1 3/4 percent.

changes.quote: The softening in the growth of aggregate demand that emerged this spring has been prolonged in large measure by weakness in financial markets and heightened uncertainty related to problems in corporate reporting and governance.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this point to explain that market stress and corporate scandals are holding back economic growth.

changes.quote: The current accommodative stance of monetary policy, coupled with still-robust underlying growth in productivity, should be sufficient to foster an improving business climate over time.
changes.explanation: The statement now emphasizes that low interest rates and strong productivity will help businesses improve over time.

changes.quote: Nonetheless, the Committee recognizes that, for the foreseeable future, against the background of its long run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness.
changes.explanation: The Fed shifted its assessment to state that future risks lean toward economic weakness rather than being balanced.

changes.quote: Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were Alan Greenspan, Chairman; William J. McDonough, Vice Chairman; Ben S. Bernanke, Susan S. Bies; Roger W. Ferguson, Jr.; Edward M. Gramlich; Jerry L. Jordan; Donald L. Kohn, Robert D. McTeer, Jr.; Mark W. Olson; Anthony M. Santomero, and Gary H. Stern.
changes.explanation: The list of voters was updated to include new participants at this meeting.

tone_quotes.quote: The softening in the growth of aggregate demand that emerged this spring has been prolonged in large measure by weakness in financial markets and heightened uncertainty related to problems in corporate reporting and governance.

Nonetheless, the Committee recognizes that, for the foreseeable future, against the background of its long run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are weighted mainly toward conditions that may generate economic weakness.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.53% APR costs about $56.38 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.12% and moved -10 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.43% would fall by about $19.63 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 5.8%, and employers added an average of -11k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.5% over the past year (July 2002); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -10 bp on the day.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed remains cautious while watching economic weakness and corporate governance issues. Upcoming decisions will depend on whether financial markets stabilize and growth picks up.
